questions.question: When did the Sarada script first emerge?
questions.solution_html:
• The Sarada script first emerged around the 8th century CE. The script is a descendant of
  • the Gupta script and belongs to the Brahmic family of scripts. It was widely used in
  • the northwestern Indian subcontinent, especially for writing Sanskrit and Kashmiri.
questions.final_answer: the northwestern Indian subcontinent, especially for writing Sanskrit and Kashmiri
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: In which way all the details in descriptive catalogues are shown?
questions.solution_html:
• In descriptive catalogs, details are presented in a structured and standardized format
  • typically in a bibliographic record. Librarians and other catalogers follow established
  • rules, such as those in Resource Description and Access (RDA), to ensure
  • consistent and accurate data for users.
questions.final_answer: consistent and accurate data for users
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is the important factor to remember for building a library?
questions.solution_html:
• The most important factor when building a library is understanding and addressing the
  • needs of the community it will serve. Rather than being a static container for books, a
  • modern library must be a flexible and welcoming community hub that meets diverse
  • educational, recreational, and social needs.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is the life span of leather or birch bark manuscripts?
questions.solution_html:
• The life span of manuscripts made from leather and birch bark varies significantly depending
  • on how they were prepared and stored. While both are organic and susceptible to decay
  • surviving artifacts prove they can last for centuries, and in exceptional conditions, for
  • millennia.

questions.question: Which method is helpful to eradicating worms and insects?
questions.solution_html:
• There are many effective methods for eradicating worms and insects, ranging from natural
  • remedies and biological controls to chemical treatments and physical barriers. The best
  • method depends on the type of pest, the location (garden, home, or body), and the
  • desired speed of results.

questions.question: Through which process we can get all the informations about a / manuscript?
questions.solution_html:
• To gain comprehensive information about a manuscript, the process of codicology is used.
  • This is the scientific study of manuscripts as physical objects and cultural artifacts
  • distinct from the study of the text itself.
questions.final_answer: distinct from the study of the text itself

questions.question: Who are known as non-institutional custodians?
questions.solution_html:
• While a "non-institutional custodian" is not a standard term in finance, it most closely refers
  • to non-custodial services and the individuals who use them. In this model, the
  • user acts as their own custodian, maintaining full control over their financial assets
  • without relying on a traditional financial institution.
questions.final_answer: without relying on a traditional financial institution
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is the place of temporary receipt in the collection of manuscript?
questions.solution_html:
• In the collection of manuscripts, a temporary receipt is not a physical location but an
  • administrative procedure and designated holding area for newly acquired items. It is part of
  • the process of intake and ensures the proper cataloging, stabilization, and transfer of
  • the manuscript to its permanent storage location within an archive or library.
questions.final_answer: the manuscript to its permanent storage location within an archive or library
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is the aim of 'Textual Criticism'?
questions.solution_html:
• The aim of textual criticism is to reconstruct the original text of a document by comparing
  • all available manuscript copies to identify and remove transcription errors and variants. This
  • scholarly practice seeks to produce a "critical edition" of the text that is as close as
  • possible to the original wording and meaning, which can then be used for other
  • literary and historical analysis.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Which method is used in Nepal to protect manuscripts
questions.solution_html:
• In Nepal, the methods used to protect manuscripts range from traditional techniques that
  • have been practiced for centuries to modern preservation and digitization efforts.
  • Institutions like the National Archives of Nepal and the Asa Archives combine these
  • approaches to preserve the country's rich written heritage.
questions.final_answer: approaches to preserve the country's rich written heritage
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is known as 'codex' of a manuscript?
questions.solution_html:
• A "codex" is a manuscript book, meaning it's a collection of handwritten pages bound
  • together along one edge, forming the ancestor of the modern book. It was a significant
  • advancement over scrolls because it allowed for easier reading, portability, and quick
  • access to different sections.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Which are the writing tools used in Manuscriptology?
questions.solution_html:
• Manuscriptology uses a variety of tools, including instruments for writing like metal styluses
  • and pens, and implements for preparing the writing surface and finishing the
  • manuscript, such as burnishers, scissors, and ink-pots. The specific tools vary
  • based on the writing material, which could be palm leaves, birch bark, or paper
  • among others.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What are the qualifications of a scribe?
questions.solution_html:
• Qualifications for a scribe vary by context but generally include a minimum educational level
  • (often high school), with specific requirements like being one academic step below the
  • candidate for examination scribes. Medical scribes need additional skills such as a strong
  • grasp of medical terminology, anatomy, and physiology, along with proficient typing and
  • computer skills.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What advantages are associated with the publication of manuscripts?
questions.solution_html:
• The publication of manuscripts provides significant advantages to the author, the academic
  • community, and society at large. It solidifies a researcher's reputation, contributes to the
  • expansion of collective knowledge, and ensures the wider dissemination of research findings
  • for the benefit of all.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Write a paragraph about the importance of manuscript libraries.
questions.solution_html:
• Manuscript libraries serve as irreplaceable repositories of human knowledge, acting as
  • crucial links to past civilizations. They meticulously preserve a vast range of original
  • handwritten documents—from scientific and religious texts to personal letters
  • diaries, and historical records—offering researchers, historians, and scholars
  • authentic, primary source materials that provide unique insights into the cultures
  • philosophies, and daily lives of past societies. Through specialized preservation and
  • conservation techniques, these libraries safeguard fragile, aged materials from
  • physical and biological deterioration, often making them available to a global
  • audience through digitization efforts. By doing so, they not only protect irreplaceable
  • artifacts from being lost forever but also ensure that this vast collective heritage
  • remains accessible for study and can inform our understanding of the present and
  • shape the future.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Which are the illustrated manuscripts found in Saraswathi Mahal / Library, Thanjavoor? Part D Essay
questions.solution_html:
• The Saraswathi Mahal Library in Thanjavur has illustrated manuscripts including
  • the Citra Ramayana, illustrated Rig Veda manuscripts, Gajasastra (elephants)
  • and Aswasastra (horses), and mythological pictures. Other illustrated items include
  • botanical specimens, military costumes, and paintings based on a study of human
  • and animal faces.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Describe the main features of writing materials in Manuscriptology.
questions.solution_html:
• In manuscriptology, the main features of writing materials relate to their physical properties
  • preparation, and durability, which all influenced a text's appearance, preservation, and
  • cultural context. Primary materials include palm leaves, birch bark, parchment, and
  • handmade paper, each with distinct characteristics.
questions.final_answer: handmade paper, each with distinct characteristics
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Which are the steps in the field work of manuscript collection.
questions.solution_html:
• The field work for manuscript collection involves several key steps, starting with planning
  • and preparation and ending with the documentation and preservation of the materials. This
  • process is complex, especially for historically significant or oral-tradition-based
  • manuscripts.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Write an essay on the significance of Manuscriptology.
questions.solution_html:
• Manuscriptology is the scientific study of handwritten documents, particularly those with
  • historical, cultural, or artistic value. This field examines the original artifacts of
  • knowledge, providing an authentic and unmediated window into the past. Through a
  • systematic process of collection, conservation, cataloging, and critical analysis
  • manuscriptology reveals historical narratives, preserves cultural heritage, and
  • informs modern research across diverse fields. In an increasingly digital world, the
  • study of these fragile, centuries-old documents is more critical than ever, as they
  • contain irreplaceable information that risks being lost forever.
questions.final_answer: contain irreplaceable information that risks being lost forever
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss about the features of Manuscript libraries.
questions.solution_html:
• Manuscript libraries specialize in the collection, preservation, and study of historical
  • handwritten documents. Their primary features center on the fragility and uniqueness of
  • their holdings, which necessitates special handling, conservation methods, and access
  • policies.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
